# Success

Authors will be able to describe and check existing tutorials without changing tools. Instructors will be able to compare requirements, validation records, and review status across engines.

The baseline records results currently documented for tutorialverse. We will update it at grant start to include any completed pilot work.

| Measure | Documented baseline | Grant-end target |
|--------------------------------|-------------------|--------------------------------|
| Adapters with capability reports | 0 demonstrated | 3 initial adapters |
| Tutorials indexed through tutorialverse | 0 demonstrated | 5–10 across supported formats |
| External reviewers of schema, adapters, or tutorials | 0 documented reviews | At least 3 |
| Example tutorials tested in CI | 0 demonstrated | 4, collectively covering all adapters |
| Integration templates | 0 demonstrated | 3–4 |
| Reusable tutorial-validation workflow | 0 demonstrated | At least 1 |

Completion also requires version 1.0 of the schema, R package, and registry, with review, governance, and stale-resource policies published and exercised in the pilot.

Validation success will mean passing the checks reported for that engine and environment. During the grant, we will track missing metadata and the work authors need to supply it, alongside external submissions and review participation. After release, validation freshness and broken links will guide maintenance; the packages represented in the registry will help identify gaps in coverage.

Future work could add adapters for other tutorial engines or connect the registry to pkgdown, R-universe, and educational catalogs. Multilingual metadata, richer accessibility checks, and instructor collections remain outside the initial funded scope.
